neighbours.label: the beat where an anecdote or parable moves to its next event: the punctuation or 'Finally' just before 'one of them…', 'a man came along…'
fire: Three travellers argued about the road for an hour. Finally, an old woman walked by and pointed the way.
The two farmers fought over the well all summer. After shouting for days, one of them proposed a deal.

A young monk asked his master about patience. The master said nothing.
The next morning, the monk found a seed on his mat.
The villagers all stood around the fallen tree, complaining. Finally, a little boy came along with a saw.
A merchant lost his purse in the market and wept. After searching for some time, a beggar handed it back.

The king asked each son to break a bundle of sticks. None could do it.
Then the youngest untied the bundle.
Two frogs fell into a bucket of cream. They kicked for hours. Finally, one of them gave up.
A man climbed to the roof of his house to wait for rescue. Soon a boat came by, and he waved it off.
quiet: The road survey lists three routes and gives the distance of each one in kilometres.
Water rights for farms in the valley are set by the regional board every summer.
Patience is often listed as a key trait for teachers and nurses.
The fallen tree blocked the road until the county crew removed it on Monday.
Market stalls must be licensed and inspected twice a year.
A bundle of sticks is stronger than a single stick, as engineers know.
Frogs can absorb water through their skin and rarely need to drink.
Roofs in flood zones should be built to carry the weight of people.
